title: Book Three · Chapter 50: One More Game
story:
On Tuesday, the park grass is dry by midmorning.

Kai and his friend bring the ball. Ronan brings Leo. They change sides twice, and nobody stays beside the same partner all morning.

Ronan sends one good pass across the grass. Leo reaches it and scores between the bags.

“At last,” Leo says.

“You needed the right pass,” Ronan answers.

Kai picks up the ball.

“And we needed a smaller goal.”

They play again. This time, Kai's friend stops Leo's next shot. The ball comes back across the grass, and Ronan has to run after it.

By the time Anna and Lin arrive, all four boys need a drink.

The girls finished their run on the park path. Anna sits beneath the tree with her bottle. Lin stays in the shade beside her.

“Four laps again?” Ronan asks.

“Different path,” Anna says. “We ran to the far gate and back twice.”

Leo asks which gate. She points through the trees. He looks along the path and nods.

Near the entrance, a woman sells cold drinks from a large box. Kai wants one.

Leo takes a few coins from his pocket. Then he looks at the price board.

“One is enough,” he says.

Ronan has money for one too. He buys his own drink. Anna and Lin keep their water, and Kai's friend chooses a smaller cup.

They sit along the wall near the shade. Leo's drink is colder than he expects. He puts the cup against his forehead.

“New hat?” Kai asks.

“A very wet one.”

Ronan laughs. Anna points to the water running down Leo's wrist.

“Your sleeve will get it next.”

Leo changes hands. Lin passes him a small piece of paper to wipe the cup.

For a little while, everyone talks at once. The cold water runs onto Ronan's fingers too. He wipes them on the paper around his cup.

Then Anna stands. She and Lin have a visit planned with another friend. They cannot stay for the whole morning.

“We promised her eleven,” Anna says.

“See you before you leave?” she asks Leo.

“Tomorrow at the bus station is early.”

“Then goodbye for now.”

She shakes his hand. Lin waves, and the girls take the path through the trees.

Kai's friend needs to go too. Kai goes with him after one last throw of the ball.

Ronan and Leo carry their empty cups to a bin.

“One more game?” Ronan asks.

Leo looks at the open grass. Kai has taken the ball.

They both laugh.

“A walk,” Leo says. “I need to buy something small for my grandmother.”

Ronan nods and goes beside him toward the shops. Leo counts the money left in his palm before he puts it away.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

score＝进球、得分；shade＝阴凉处；forehead＝额头；palm＝手掌。

## 理解问题

1. 这天踢球的搭档怎样变化？Anna和Lin为什么不能一直留下？
2. Leo怎样按自己的钱选择饮料？最后为什么不能再来一局球？

## 读句子

**Kai has taken the ball.**

拆开看：Kai / has taken / the ball.

Kai／已经带走了／球。
